geology_notes: Churchill Resources holds the Foxtrot past-producing antimony mine (Frost Cove / Black Raven property) in central Newfoundland, augmented by the March 2026 Golden Baie option (39,925 ha, TSXV-approved March 27, 2026) and a Black Raven LOI. Confirmed geological highlights from accessible disclosures: (1) FC25-27: 13.00% Sb over 0.57m at Frost Cove (validated in the May 2026 data-correction release that downgraded the broader initial assay dataset); (2) a second new polymetallic system at southern Frost Cove / Black Raven yielding 7.25% Sb over 1.98m; (3) a 20-vein Au-Ag-Mo-Pb-Zn swarm at Pomley Cove Pond with surface channel results including 17.3 g/t Au and 130 g/t Ag; (4) zinc grab samples at Black Raven reaching 5.25%, 11.03%, and 12.11% Zn with associated Au, Ag, and Pb. Nine 2026 drill holes reported completed circa July 13; as of August 5, 2026, assay results are twenty-three days past the 'imminent' announcement with no results headline indexed in searches conducted today. The August 2023 NI 43-101 technical report remains the most recent on file; the extraction yielded no compliant resource estimate — all five resource/reserve fields are null per the extraction. Score of 3 reflects confirmed high-grade multi-commodity mineralisation across a consolidated and expanding NL property package, constrained by the absence of a compliant resource estimate and twenty-three days of post-drill assay silence.

catalyst_notes: Macro catalyst: China's September 2024 antimony export controls restricted supply from the dominant global producer and have sustained Western-government urgency for domestic and allied critical mineral supply chains. August 5, 2026 web search confirms DoD funding to domestic US antimony projects remains active (over USD $59M to Perpetua Resources' Stibnite project; a $43.4M DPA grant to Alaska Range Resources awarded September 2025). Antimony is named in Canada's Critical Minerals Strategy and on the US Defense Production Act designated minerals list, making Foxtrot a credible candidate for NRCan/provincial grant support and strategic partnership interest. This macro tailwind remains structurally intact. Company-specific catalyst (adverse): CRI shares fell approximately 20% on July 15, 2026, closing near C$0.04. The specific trigger remains unconfirmed despite repeated searches — no explanatory headline has been indexed. The timing (two days after the nine 2026 drill holes were reported completed circa July 13) is notable. As of August 5, the 2026 assay batch is twenty-three days past the 'imminent' announcement with no results headline indexed. Score of 2 maintained: the macro tailwind is intact and durable, but an unexplained 20% stock decline, a CEO transition mid-program, and twenty-three days of assay silence past 'imminent' constitute accumulating near-term negative signals that cap the catalyst score.
